drills.title: Fit a least squares line
drills.prompt:
Fit the least squares line $\hat y = b_0 + b_1x$ to these five points, and find $r^2$
(4 decimals each).

$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & {x1} & {x2} & {x3} & {x4} & {x5} \\ \hline y & {y1:num1} & {y2:num1} & {y3:num1} & {y4:num1} & {y5:num1} \end{array}$$
drills.solution:
$\bar x = {xb:num4}$, $\bar y = {yb:num4}$, $S_{xx} = {sxx:num4}$, $S_{xy} = {sxy:num4}$, $S_{yy} = {syy:num4}$.

$b_1 = S_{xy}/S_{xx} =$ **{b1:num4}**, $b_0 = \bar y - b_1\bar x =$ **{b0:num4}**, and
$r^2 = S_{xy}^2/(S_{xx}S_{yy}) =$ **{rsq:num4}**.

drills.title: t test for the slope from summary statistics
drills.prompt:
A regression on $n = {nn}$ points has $S_{xx} = {sxx}$, $S_{xy} = {sxy:num1}$ and $S_{yy} = {syy:num1}$.
Test $H_0: \beta_1 = 0$ against $H_1: \beta_1 \ne 0$. Find $b_1$ (4 decimals), the $t$ statistic
(3 decimals) and the p-value (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
$b_1 = S_{xy}/S_{xx} =$ **{b1:num4}**. $\text{SSE} = S_{yy} - b_1S_{xy} = {sse:num4}$, so
$s = \sqrt{\text{SSE}/(n-2)} = \sqrt{{sse:num4}/{dfree}} = {s:num4}$ and $\text{SE}(b_1) = s/\sqrt{S_{xx}} = {se:num4}$.

$t = b_1/\text{SE}(b_1) =$ **{tt:dp3}** on {dfree} df; two-sided p-value $\approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: Confidence and prediction intervals at x0
drills.prompt:
A regression on $n = {nn}$ points gives $\hat y = {b0v:num2} {b1v:signedcoef}x$, with $s = {sres:num2}$,
$\bar x = {xbar:num1}$ and $S_{xx} = {sxx}$. At $x_0 = {x0:num1}$, find $\hat y_0$, the half-width of the
95% confidence interval for the mean response, and the half-width of the 95% prediction interval
for a new observation (3 decimals each).
drills.solution:
$\hat y_0 = {b0v:num2} {b1v:signed}({x0:num1}) =$ **{yh:dp3}**. With {dfree} df, $t_{0.025} = {ts:dp3}$, and
$\dfrac1n + \dfrac{(x_0 - \bar x)^2}{S_{xx}} = {kk:num4}$.

Mean response: ${ts:dp3}({sres:num2})\sqrt{{kk:num4}} =$ **{hci:dp3}**.
New observation: ${ts:dp3}({sres:num2})\sqrt{1 + {kk:num4}} =$ **{hpi:dp3}**.

drills.title: One-way ANOVA from raw data

calc.sse: 3*(variance(g11, g12, g13, g14) + variance(g21, g22, g23, g24) + variance(g31, g32, g33, g34))

drills.prompt:
Three treatments are each applied to four units:

$$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{A} & {g11} & {g12} & {g13} & {g14} \\ \text{B} & {h1} & {h2} & {h3} & {h4} \\ \text{C} & {g31} & {g32} & {g33} & {g34} \end{array}$$

Find SSTr, SSE and the $F$ statistic (3 decimals each) and the p-value (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
Group means {m1:num4}, {m2:num4}, {m3:num4}; grand mean {gm:num4}.
$\text{SSTr} = 4\sum(\bar y_i - \bar y)^2 =$ **{sstr:dp3}**; $\text{SSE} = \sum\sum(y_{ij} - \bar y_i)^2 =$ **{sse:dp3}**.

$\text{MSTr} = {sstr:dp3}/2 = {mstr:dp3}$, $\text{MSE} = {sse:dp3}/9 = {mse:dp3}$, so $F =$ **{ff:dp3}** on (2, 9) df,
and the p-value is $P(F_{2,9} \ge {ff:dp3}) \approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: One-way ANOVA from summary statistics
drills.prompt:
Three independent groups give:

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & \text{group 1} & \text{group 2} & \text{group 3} \\ \hline n_i & {n1} & {n2} & {n3} \\ \bar y_i & {m1:num1} & {m2:num1} & {m3:num1} \\ s_i & {s1:num1} & {s2:num1} & {s3:num1} \end{array}$$

Find the ANOVA $F$ statistic (3 decimals) and its p-value (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
$N = {bign}$; weighted grand mean $= \sum n_i\bar y_i/N = {gm:num4}$.
$\text{SSTr} = \sum n_i(\bar y_i - \bar y)^2 = {sstr:dp3}$ and $\text{SSE} = \sum(n_i - 1)s_i^2 = {sse:dp3}$.

$\text{MSTr} = {sstr:dp3}/2 = {mstr:dp3}$, $\text{MSE} = {sse:dp3}/{dfe} = {mse:dp3}$, so $F =$ **{ff:dp3}** on (2, {dfe}) df,
with p-value $\approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: Complete an ANOVA table
drills.prompt:
A one-way ANOVA compares {kk} groups of {ng} observations each. The treatment sum of squares is
$\text{SSTr} = {sstr:num1}$ and the total sum of squares is $\text{SST} = {sst:num1}$. Find MSE and $F$
(3 decimals each) and the p-value (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
$N = {bign}$. Degrees of freedom: treatments $k - 1 = {df1}$, error $N - k = {df2}$, total {dft}.
$\text{SSE} = \text{SST} - \text{SSTr} = {sse2:num1}$, so $\text{MSE} = {sse2:num1}/{df2} =$ **{mse:dp3}**.

$\text{MSTr} = {sstr:num1}/{df1} = {mstr:dp3}$, $F = {mstr:dp3}/{mse:dp3} =$ **{ff:dp3}**, and
the p-value is $P(F_{{df1},{df2}} \ge {ff:dp3}) \approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: Sign test p-value
drills.prompt:
In a paired study of {nn} units, {kk} differences are positive, {neg} are negative and {zz} are exactly
zero. Use the sign test of $H_0$: median difference $= 0$ against $H_1$: median difference $> 0$.
Find the p-value (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
Drop the {zz} zero differences, leaving $n = {nz}$. Under $H_0$ the number of positive signs is
$B \sim \text{Bin}({nz}, 1/2)$, so the p-value is $P(B \ge {kk}) = 1 - P(B \le {km1}) \approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
drills.prompt:
Eight paired differences are
$${d1:num1},\ {d2:num1},\ {d3:num1},\ {d4:num1},\ {d5:num1},\ {d6:num1},\ {d7:num1},\ {d8:num1}$$
Find the Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic $W^+$, its normal-approximation $z$ (no continuity correction,
3 decimals) and the one-sided p-value for $H_1$: median $> 0$ (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
Rank the absolute values from 1 to 8. The ranks of the differences, in the order given, are
{r1}, {r2}, {r3}, {r4}, {r5}, {r6}, {r7}, {r8}. Adding the ranks of the positive differences gives
$W^+ =$ **{wp}** (and $W^- = {wm}$; the two add to 36).

Under $H_0$, $E(W^+) = 8 \cdot 9/4 = 18$ and $\operatorname{Var}(W^+) = 8 \cdot 9 \cdot 17/24 = 51$, so
$z = ({wp} - 18)/\sqrt{51} =$ **{zz:dp3}** and the p-value is $P(Z \ge {zz:dp3}) \approx$ **{pv:num4}**.

drills.title: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
drills.prompt:
Sample A: {a1}, {a2}, {a3}, {a4}, {a5}. Sample B: {b1}, {b2}, {b3}, {b4}, {b5}.
Rank all ten values together (1 = smallest). Find the rank sum $W$ of sample A, the Mann–Whitney
$U = W - 15$, and the one-sided normal-approximation p-value for $H_1$: A is shifted upward (no continuity
correction, 4 decimals).
drills.solution:
The ranks of A's values are {ra1}, {ra2}, {ra3}, {ra4}, {ra5}, so $W =$ **{ww}** and $U = {ww} - 15 =$ **{uu}**.

Under $H_0$, $E(W) = 5 \cdot 11/2 = 27.5$ and $\operatorname{Var}(W) = 5 \cdot 5 \cdot 11/12 = 22.917$, so
$z = ({ww} - 27.5)/\sqrt{22.917} = {zz:dp3}$ and the p-value is $P(Z \ge {zz:dp3}) \approx$ **{pv:num4}**.
